title: Inductive theories: unions and universal-existential axioms

based_on.title: Model Theory Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 53–56 (§5.4, directed unions, Proposition 5.14 and Theorem 5.15; supporting diagram methods pp. 50–52; updated 2018-12-14)

summary: Characterize theories closed under increasing unions by axioms that ask for witnesses after arbitrary finite choices.
abstract: An increasing union of orders with no greatest element still has no greatest element: each point already has a larger point at a stage where it occurs. A greatest element behaves differently. Every finite initial segment of the natural numbers has a last point, while their union has none. We characterize the first-order theories whose models survive increasing unions. They are exactly those that can be axiomatized by universal choices followed by existential witnesses, with a quantifier-free condition on the choices and witnesses. The proof explains how compactness turns closure under unions into this particular form of axioms, and why ordinary substructure inclusions suffice even when they preserve fewer formulas than elementary embeddings.
